Notes
Cloud Migration

Configure your Supabase credentials in this file, then use the tools below.

Not tested
Last Sync: Never
Push to Cloud sends everything currently in this browser up to Supabase — use it after Restore Academy to make a recovered backup durable, or any time you suspect the cloud has fallen out of sync. It never deletes anything from the cloud. Create Logins for Everyone sets up a login for every current student and teacher with an email set — their own email, and their ID as the password — safe to click more than once, already-created logins are updated in place. Admins are managed separately below.
Add Administrator
Creates a real login for a new administrator — they'll sign in with this email and the shared admin password.
Migrate Existing Staff Login
For an admin or teacher who already had a login before this scheme — resets their account to the current one (admin: shared admin password; teacher: their own ID as the password). Safe to run again if unsure whether it already happened.
Clean Up Redundant Multi-Course Logins
A student in two courses now logs in once and can switch between both — before this, each course had its own separate login. Run this once to remove any old, now-redundant logins left over from before. Safe to run any time; only touches accounts that are genuinely redundant.
Data Health Check
Scans for data that's fallen out of sync or is inconsistent — orphaned records (a lesson whose student no longer exists, a broken multi-course link), duplicate lessons, teacher double-bookings, rooms over capacity, a frozen student still on the calendar, paid payroll periods worth double-checking for the double-session bug, unsynced records, and (when connected) duplicate or stale-linked rows in Supabase itself. Read-only: it only reports issues, it never changes or deletes anything on its own.
Reconnect Orphaned Lessons
Some lessons lost their link to the student they belong to — they still hold the student's name, but point at an id that no longer exists, so the student looks like they have no lessons and their slot still shows as taken. This finds each orphaned lesson and works out which student it belongs to, matching on name + teacher + instrument together — never name alone. Preview lists exactly what it would reconnect and what it can't safely decide; nothing changes until you review it and confirm.
Rebuild Deleted Students
For students whose record was deleted entirely but whose lessons survived. Those lessons are the last remaining record of that person, and they still carry enough to rebuild one: name, teacher, instrument, and their usual day & time. What cannot be recovered — because it only ever lived on the deleted record — is phone, email, age, joined date, plan & pricing, and payment history. Rebuilt students are created on the default monthly plan and flagged for review, so check each one's plan and price before invoicing. Preview changes nothing.
Fix Duplicate Student Codes
Two different problems share this symptom. Where the same person appears more than once, the copies are merged into the earliest record — lessons, payments and homework move across first, then the extra copies are removed. Where different people ended up sharing one code, nobody is deleted: the earliest keeps the code and the others are issued fresh unused ones. Duplicate codes are what make an Edit click, or a newly-scheduled lesson, land on the wrong student, so fixing this resolves that class of problem at its source. Preview changes nothing.
Link One Person's Separate Courses
For a student taking two courses whose records were created before the "+ Add Another Course" feature existed — they currently show as two unrelated students. Linking makes them read "Course 1 of 2" and count as one person in your student total, while keeping each course's lessons, payments and payroll fully separate. Nothing is merged or deleted. Only records with the same name and a genuinely different course (instrument, teacher or day) are offered — identical records are true duplicates and belong in the tool above instead.
Clean Duplicate Rows in Supabase
The tool above fixes your local records; this one cleans the Supabase table itself, where the duplicate rows actually live. Rows count as the same person only when name, teacher and instrument all match — so a student with two genuine courses is never collapsed — and at least one row always survives for everyone. The row kept is the one this app already points at, or failing that the earliest. Back up before applying.
Reconnect Orphaned Lesson Logs
Homework and lesson notes that lost their link to the lesson they belong to — the notes are intact, they just stopped appearing on the student's profile. Each log still records the student name and lesson date, and is re-linked only when that pair matches exactly one lesson; anything ambiguous is left for you. Preview changes nothing.
For logs with no matching lesson at all — the note itself is still there, it just has nothing to attach to. Creates a new lesson marked Attended, on the log's own date, only for a student its name + teacher + instrument identify uniquely. No payment or amount is ever created — this only gives the note somewhere to live again.
Fix Duplicate Lessons
The same student billed or logged twice on one date. Identical duplicates and a leftover "Scheduled" placeholder superseded by a real recorded outcome are merged automatically. Two DIFFERENT real outcomes on the same day (e.g. Excused vs. Attended) are a genuine conflict only you can resolve — you'll get a picker for each. This also clears up several of the "ambiguous" cases in the tool above, since some of that ambiguity was caused by these duplicates in the first place.
Bulk Resolve Old Make-ups
Clears a backlog of stale owed make-ups dated before a chosen date, without reviewing each one individually. Uses the exact same "Already Made Up" resolution as the Details button on the Makeup Dashboard — the lesson, its attendance record, and payroll are untouched; only the owed status clears. Nothing is ever deleted.
Resolve Misassigned Make-ups
Finds owed make-ups that are definitively wrong — either dated before the linked student even registered, or the lesson's own recorded name doesn't match who its id resolves to now. Both only happen from a reused/misassigned student id, never from a genuine session, so no cutoff date is needed. Same safe resolution as above: only the owed status clears, nothing is deleted.
Deletion Log
Every student removal recorded on this device — who, when, and why — with a full snapshot so any of them can be restored exactly as they were. Also catches students that disappear from the cloud without being deleted here (they're kept and re-uploaded automatically, and logged so you know it happened).
Archive Lessons Before a Date
Gives a clean launch point by hiding every lesson before a chosen date. Archived lessons drop out of dashboards, make-up counts, attendance and calculations exactly as deleting them would — but nothing is destroyed, and the Restore button brings the whole batch back. Old lessons are the only surviving trace of some students and underpin past revenue/payroll history, which is why this archives rather than deletes.
Compare Backup to Live Data
Load a backup JSON to see exactly what's missing from the current data — students, lessons, and any records still pointing at students who no longer exist. Read-only: this changes nothing, it only reports. The Deletion Log can only record removals made from this app, so a cloud-side delete leaves no trace there; comparing against a backup taken before the loss is the way to see those.
Fix Course Instrument / Teacher Mismatches
Finds upcoming lessons carrying a different instrument or teacher than the course they belong to — which makes a two-course student show two identical-looking rows in the Attendance Ledger, and credits the wrong teacher in payroll. Only future scheduled lessons are corrected; past sessions keep whatever was actually recorded.
Link Unlinked Multi-Course Students
Finds same-name students taking genuinely different courses who aren't connected — so they count as two people in your student total and don't show the "Course 1 of 2" badge. Only the connection changes; lessons, payments and payroll are untouched.
Post-Reset Cleanup
Four tools for the specific mess a database reset leaves behind, when students are re-entered by hand and their real history is typed back in around them. Each previews before changing anything.
1 · Fix Start Dates Earlier Than Their Own Lessons
A re-entered student's Starting Date is the day they were re-typed, not the day they actually started — so their real earlier lessons look impossible and trip the "reused student id" warning. This moves each Starting Date back to that student's own earliest lesson. No lesson, payment or payroll record is touched.
2 · Remove Lesson Logs With No Lesson
Only logs with no matching lesson at all. Anything re-linkable is automatically excluded and handled by Reconnect Orphaned Lesson Logs above instead — so this can't throw away a log whose session still exists. Everything removed goes to the Deletion Log and can be restored.
3 · Clear Payment Snapshots With No Payment
Left behind when a month is un-marked, or when lessons are entered to correct payroll without a payment attached. They affect no revenue figure — clearing them only stops a stale amount being read back if that month is ever marked paid later.
4 · Re-link Waiting-List Entries to Re-entered Students
An entry pointing at a student id that no longer exists, where someone of the same name is back under a new one. Re-linking keeps the entry and their place in the queue.
5 · Update Lesson Names Left Over From a Rename
Renaming a student now updates their lessons automatically, but any rename done before that left its lessons carrying the old name. This splits them in two: near-identical names (a spelling fix) can be updated in bulk, while names too different to be the same person are listed for you to check by hand — those may be genuinely misassigned lessons, and relabelling them would hide a real problem.
